scenarioStory.history: Discharged home yesterday after a STEMI treated with emergent PCI and stent placement three days ago. Wife found him this afternoon pale, weak, and short of breath sitting on the edge of the bed, unable to walk to the bathroom without nearly collapsing. He denies chest pain currently but reports feeling 'wiped out' and lightheaded when he tries to stand.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 68-year-old male three days post-MI, pale and diaphoretic, sitting on the edge of the bed leaning forward. He is weak, mildly dyspneic, with cool mottled skin and weak peripheral pulses, consistent with early cardiogenic shock. → IV access, ASA, and cautious fluid bolus given: Crew places IV access, applies the cardiac monitor and defib pads, obtains a 12-lead EKG, gives aspirin, and administers a cautious 250-500 mL fluid bolus given the hypotension, while watching closely for signs of fluid overload before considering any repeat bolus. → Fluid-refractory, norepinephrine started: Blood pressure remains low despite the cautious fluid bolus and crackles are unchanged. The crew withholds further fluid, initiates a norepinephrine infusion titrated to blood pressure, and provides advance notification to the receiving hospital. → Perfusion improves, transport initiated: Blood pressure has improved on the titrated norepinephrine infusion. The patient is transported with serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment to a facility capable of managing post-MI cardiogenic shock.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Weakness and shortness of breath, three days after a heart attack

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 68-year-old male three days post-MI, pale and diaphoretic, sitting on the edge of the bed leaning forward. He is weak, mildly dyspneic, with cool mottled skin and weak peripheral pulses, consistent with early cardiogenic shock.

scenarioEvents.name: IV access, ASA, and cautious fluid bolus given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew places IV access, applies the cardiac monitor and defib pads, obtains a 12-lead EKG, gives aspirin, and administers a cautious 250-500 mL fluid bolus given the hypotension, while watching closely for signs of fluid overload before considering any repeat bolus.
relatedChecklist: Establish IV access; if unable within 2 attempts/90 seconds, place an IO
Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes; transmit for STEMI interpretation
Give a cautious 250-500 mL IV fluid bolus given SBP <100 mmHg
Place defibrillator pads and maintain continuous cardiac monitoring
Reassess breath sounds and JVD before considering any repeat fluid bolus

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid-refractory, norepinephrine started
scenarioEvents.description: Blood pressure remains low despite the cautious fluid bolus and crackles are unchanged. The crew withholds further fluid, initiates a norepinephrine infusion titrated to blood pressure, and provides advance notification to the receiving hospital.
relatedChecklist: Start norepinephrine infusion at 1.8 mcg/min (90 kg × 0.02 mcg/kg/min); titrate to SBP >90 mmHg
Provide advance notification to the receiving hospital

scenarioEvents.name: Perfusion improves, transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Blood pressure has improved on the titrated norepinephrine infusion. The patient is transported with serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment to a facility capable of managing post-MI cardiogenic shock.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and neurologic status serially en route, at least every 15 minutes

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid bolus repeated without reassessment
scenarioEvents.description: The crew repeats the fluid bolus without reassessing breath sounds or JVD. The underlying cardiogenic pulmonary edema worsens, with increasing crackles, hypoxia, and respiratory distress.
relatedChecklist: Recognize iatrogenic pulmonary edema; stop fluids, support ventilation, start norepinephrine
